messages.content: 尋找海平面下5000米處水的沸點和熔點。

function.name: get_boiling_melting_points
function.description: Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

The user wants boiling point and melting point of water at sea level 5000 meters? Actually "海平面下5000米處" means at altitude 5000 meters below sea level? Wait "海平面下5000米處" could mean at 5000 meters below sea level (i.e., depth). But water at depth? They might mean at altitude 5000 meters above sea level? The phrase "海平面下" means below sea level. But maybe they want at 5000 meters below sea level? That would be deep ocean. But the question: "尋找海平面下5000米處水的沸點和熔點。" Means "Find the boiling point and melting point of water at 5000 meters below sea level." So we need to compute boiling point at that pressure. At depth 5000 m, pressure is about 1 atm + 10 atm per km? Actually hydrostatic pressure increases ~1 atm per 10 m? Wait 1 atm ~101.3 kPa. Pressure increase per meter of water column: ρgh = 1000 kg/m3 * 9.81 m/s2 * 1 m = 9.81 kPa per meter. So 10 m gives ~98 kPa ~1 atm. So 5000 m gives ~49 atm? Actually 5000 m * 9.81 kPa/m = 49050 kPa = 490.5 atm? Wait 49050 kPa / 101.3 kPa/atm = 484 atm. So huge pressure. Boiling point increases with pressure. At 5000 m depth, water will not boil until extremely high temperature. But melting point also changes slightly with pressure. But at such high pressure, water may become supercritical? Actually critical point of water is at 22.064 MPa (~218 atm) and 647 K (~374°C). At 5000 m depth, pressure ~490 atm > 218 atm, so water is supercritical. So no distinct boiling or melting points. So answer: at 5000 m below sea level, water is supercritical; no distinct boiling or melting points. Provide explanation.

We can use function get_boiling_melting_points? It expects substance name and sea_level. But we need sea_level? The function likely calculates boiling and melting points at given sea level? Actually the function signature: get_boiling_melting_points(substance, sea_level). Sea_level is number. So we can call with sea_level=5000? But the function might compute at that sea level? But we don't know implementation. We can call it. Let's call with substance="water", sea_level=5000.
